t1_annular_resolution.claim: im(A) = ker(C); attachment residual is zero at every phase and resolution

t2_soft_attachment.claim: a finite penalty leaves O(1/lambda) drift; exact assembly does not

t3_gauge_ablation.claim: distinct parameter triples generate identical trajectories; only the two centering gauges select the true one

p4_periodicity_phase.claim: Fourier motion closes the cycle; the warp is a degree-one circle map

t5_identifiability.claim: identifiability requires ker(J_C) and ker(J_E) to intersect trivially

e1_synthetic_recovery.claim: known pose and circular phase are recovered under the intended noise regime

e5_baseline_ladder.claim: joint gauge-fixed inference with exact coupling improves held-out cross-modal prediction and interface validity over the locked alternatives

verdict.reproducibility_note: An arm whose smallest non-gauge eigenvalue is far below the full model's sits in a nearly flat valley, so which point the regularizer settles on depends on floating-point rounding. Observed directly: across two machines the tee_only arm reproduced its held-out TEE error to 1e-13 but its held-out CMR extrapolation to only 1e-1. Cross-modal numbers from weakly identified arms should be read as indicative, not as reproducible measurements.
verdict.interpretation_of_the_gauge_comparison: A null result for full versus joint_exact_no_gauges on held-out error is the predicted outcome, not a failure. Theorem 3 concerns uniqueness of the identity/motion/session split conditional on the trajectories; removing the gauges leaves the trajectory space, and therefore the predictions, unchanged. What the gauges buy is visible in the alpha column instead: without them the identity and the common session mode trade off freely, so the arm's smallest non-gauge eigenvalue collapses to zero and the decomposition is unidentifiable even though it predicts just as well. That is the purpose the baseline lock assigns this arm, to test identifiability rather than generic fusion. Parameter recovery is measured separately in t3_gauge_ablation.

t5t6_solver_jacobian.claim: the only null directions of the fitted problem are the predicted gauges; restricted to the non-gauge tangent space it is identifiable

e6_image_domain.claim: the CMR plane and TEE sector likelihood operators drive the joint fit and improve error on hidden planes and hidden phases

verdict.rotation_is_the_weak_variable: Translation, held-out planes and held-out phases improve on every seed, but rotation does not reliably improve. Rotation is observable only through the TEE sector, and at this grid density the angular evidence is thin. A finer sector or an explicitly angular term is the next thing to try; the section 7.6 rotation gate is currently met by margin rather than by improvement.
verdict.cost_is_the_limiting_factor: A central-difference Jacobian needs two renders per parameter per iteration, so only pose, circular phase, and the leading shape modes are refined here. A full image-domain joint solve needs an analytic or adjoint gradient, which is not implemented.

e9_posterior_calibration.claim: a gauge-restricted Laplace posterior propagated to scalar measurements yields split-conformal intervals with near-nominal coverage

verdict.one_sided_criterion_note: Split conformal guarantees coverage at least the target in finite samples, so over-coverage is correct conservative behaviour and only under-coverage is a failure. The two-sided five-point criterion in the protocol marks valid conservative intervals as miscalibrated, so the one-sided fraction is reported alongside it.
verdict.coverage_resolution_note: The protocol's five-point criterion is below what this many cases can resolve: the binomial standard error on a 0.90 target at about twenty evaluation cases is already six points. The fraction within one standard error is the honest statistic at this sample size, and a real calibration claim needs the hundreds of cases the protocol assumes.
verdict.caveat: Coverage is measured on synthetic cases drawn from the same generator as the calibration half, so this demonstrates the machinery, not calibration under distribution shift. The protocol requires the locked test family and an external centre before any coverage claim is made.

e10_family_generalization.claim: in-distribution accuracy does not by itself establish robustness to a different generator

verdict.headline: Exact attachment is a structural property and holds under every family. Accuracy is not structural: held-out error and circular phase recovery degrade substantially once the generator stops matching the solver's assumptions, and the section 7.6 phase gate is missed on the held-out families. This is the honest limit of every other number in this campaign.
